items.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013
items.q: So I had to really be strong and Eddie Gladden and I had to really work well together, and when George came in we were one.

ctx.x: Well said. Let me run a couple of names by you and see if they strike you as, what did you learn from them or learn not to do, or anything in particular. Dexter Gordon?

Wow. Powerful. Imposing. He was an imposing figure when he played it was huge. All his ideas were incredibly clear. And so I had to be clear with him at all times. And he wanted it to be powerful under him as a unit. So I had to really be strong and Eddie Gladden and I had to really work well together, and when George came in we were one. He demanded it the way he played. And when you heard it, then it became the quartet. Not four people playing at the same time, or Dexter playing and the trio was playing behind…
Dexter always seemed like he was a master at playing behind the beat it seemed to me.
